title: Momentum-Locked Edge Excitons in 2D Molecular Crystals
authors: Sidhartha Nayak, Alex Boeglin, Quentin Stein, Katharina Kaiser, Guillaume Schull, Thomas Frederiksen, Tomáš Neuman
abstract: In molecular crystals, molecular excitations can hybridize into collective Frenkel excitons. Here we show that doubly degenerate excitations in planar two-dimensional molecular crystals generate excitonic bands with nontrivial momentum-resolved topological characteristics and edge states appearing only for selected crystallographic terminations. Using a model inspired by aggregates of zinc phthalocyanine molecules deposited on insulating surfaces, we demonstrate that the existence of edge excitons depends sensitively on the crystallographic orientation of the boundary and is governed by the Zak phase of the underlying bulk bands. The resulting edge states exhibit momentum-locked elliptical polarization textures originating from the internal structure of the molecular excitations, potentially enabling directional optical coupling and excitation transport. Our results establish a route toward topological and polarization-textured excitonic states in two-dimensional molecular materials.
summary: This work theoretically investigates topological properties in excitonic bands within 2D molecular crystals. By calculating the Zak phase, the authors demonstrate that edge states, which possess momentum-locked elliptical polarization, only appear for specific crystallographic boundaries. This establishes a pathway for designing directional optical coupling in molecular materials.
main_problem: The study investigates the topological characteristics and edge states of excitonic bands formed in planar two-dimensional molecular crystals.
main_result: The existence of edge excitons is shown to depend sensitively on the crystallographic boundary orientation and is governed by the Zak phase of the bulk bands, exhibiting momentum-locked elliptical polarization.
method: The authors employed theoretical modeling using a lattice Hamiltonian, calculating the Berry and Zak phases along paths in the Brillouin zone, and analyzing the resulting band structures.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using molecular excitations (e.g., zinc phthalocyanine) in 2D molecular crystals, treated via an excitonic Hamiltonian incorporating un-screened Coulomb interactions.
key_observables: Zak phase ($\gamma_{Zak}$), Berry phase ($\gamma$), momentum-resolved excitonic bands, and elliptical polarization textures.
important_parameters: Crystallographic termination/orientation, lattice structure (square lattice), and the degeneracy points ($\Gamma$ and $M$) in the Brillouin zone.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations for the Coulomb integral and neglects vibronic effects; linear dispersion alone is insufficient to confirm Dirac topology when long-range interactions are present.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the band structure along high-symmetry paths, the calculated Zak phase values for different edge terminations, and the polarization texture of the resulting edge states.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the model Hamiltonian, calculating the bulk band topology via the Zak phase, demonstrating the emergence of edge states dependent on boundary conditions, and finally characterizing the polarization texture of these topological edge states.
why_interesting: The connection between molecular excitons, topological invariants (Zak phase), and directional optical coupling provides a solid theoretical framework for engineering light-matter interactions in solid-state quantum emitters.
